summary: Iter-9 retest of Twilio X-Twilio-Signature validation after the `_public_url_for_signature` fix in twilio_service.py. Extended /app/backend/tests/test_iter8_security.py::TestSEC004_Signature: (a) fall-open with no auth_token, (b) reject when auth_token set + no signature (no consent transition recorded), (c) accept when a valid signature is computed against the PUBLIC URL (REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL) — this was the sole failure in iter-8 and is now GREEN; also verified that a STOP body creates a fresh opt-out row in db.consent_events. (d) NEW negative check: valid signature computed for a DIFFERENT URL (?foo=bar appended) is refused and no consent event is recorded — confirms the validator is actually verifying, not accepting anything. All 5 tests pass in 3.97s.
critical_code_review_comments: twilio_service._public_url_for_signature correctly rebuilds URL from X-Forwarded-Proto/Host with sensible fallbacks to request.url.scheme/netloc. Trust is scoped to signature validation only (not global proxy-header middleware) which is the safer choice.

Note: the helper does not lowercase the forwarded host. If an upstream proxy ever sent a mixed-case Host, Twilio's canonical signing (which uses whatever URL was configured in the Twilio console) would still match because it's a byte-for-byte compare of the URL string. Non-issue in practice but worth remembering.

rca of the issue: Iter-8 SEC-004c failure RCA: FastAPI's `request.url` reflected the internal uvicorn socket (http://<cluster-hostname>) whereas Twilio signs the public https URL. Fix landed in twilio_service._public_url_for_signature which reads X-Forwarded-Proto + X-Forwarded-Host from the ingress and reconstructs `<proto>://<host><path>[?<query>]`. Confirmed via tests: (c) signature for the public URL now validates; (d) signature for a wrong URL still fails, proving verification is active.
